content.intro: Learn ERB and Exploring the Standard Library through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding erb and exploring the standard library helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: ERB and Exploring the Standard Library helps you reason about embedded ruby templates. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Embedded Ruby templates. Then connect it to Standard-library documentation. The remaining syllabus points—Choosing supported libraries for a task, Understanding which libraries require explicit loading—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports erb and exploring the standard library. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for erb and exploring the standard library using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Understanding which libraries require explicit loading), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` in a folder where you may create files. The example removes notes.txt after reading it. If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain erb and exploring the standard library, identify its place in files, input/output, and the standard library, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
